chunks: Praise be to Allah, known without being seen,
Who has ever been existing, permanent;
since there was no sky with domes,
He is the Originator of creation and their Master.
He is the God of the creation and its feeder.
The sun and the moon are steadily moving in pursuit of His will.
They make every fresh thing old and every distant thing near.

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ: Known (by attributes/signs) without being physically seen
key_terms.وَارِثُهُ: His heir / The One who inherits after creation

ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of Allah described in the opening of Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited as part of the 'Supplication of the Opening' (Du'a al-Fath), reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Allah's transcendence (Tanzih) by negating physical limitations such as sight or deliberation. It contextualizes the pre-creation state to highlight God's absolute sovereignty, where celestial bodies like the sun and moon are depicted not as independent entities but as diligent servants executing divine will.
